title: On-call playbook: coordinated response for model rollout degradation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description: After a Canary rollout of model v3.14 we observed two classes of regressions: a) increased tail latency and token-level timeouts for long-context requests, and b) semantic degradations where hallucination rate for a financial customer spiked. The regression surfaced in Hosted canaries first, then surfaced in Dedicated reservations and one Private on-prem cluster after automated rollout policies began traffic migration. This ticket captures the on-call runbook, cross-team coordination steps, and post-incident actions to reduce time-to-rollback and prevent incorrect rollforwards.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported service errors and errant outputs. Latency SLO breaches occurred for 6% of requests (p95->p99 delay), and one Dedicated customer opened an escalation citing incorrect outputs in production-facing recommender flows.
symptoms_observed: p99 latency increased from 220ms to 980ms for generation route
elevated error budget consumption on hosted us-west-2 canary
customer-facing hallucination rate increased on financial prompts
KV cache mismatch logs present for quantized kernel path
initial_detection: 2025-02-14 09:12 UTC: Hosted canary alerts triggered by SLO monitor. Pager duty rotation contacted oncall, initial triage by runtime team identified a kernel selection mismatch for the new quantized artifact.
triage_notes: Confirmed regression reproduced against v3.14 with long-context test harness
Observed different behavior when running unquantized model vs quantized variant on same hardware
No infra capacity alerts; CPU/GPU utilization within expected range
Routing policy applied canary traffic to 5% initially, but an automated ramp misfired on Dedicated due to a config flag (rollout.auto_ramp=true)
actions_taken: Pinned all Hosted traffic back to v3.13 by flipping model routing flag (policy:model_pin) at 2025-02-14 09:45 UTC
Opened hotfix branch runtime/rollback-9134 to ensure deterministic kernel selection for quantized models
Engaged sales/CS to notify affected Dedicated/Private customers with targeted messaging and mitigation steps
Disabled auto_ramp for Dedicated pools and paused Private rollout jobs in orchestration control plane
customer_notifications: Email draft sent to enterprise-cs@redwood.ai for Dedicated customers
Private deployment playbook dispatched to SE contact for ACME-Finance (per-customer runbook)
rollback_plan: Primary: Immediate traffic pin to last-known-good model (v3.13) + disable auto-ramp. Secondary: If pin fails, revert kernel selection to non-quantized execution path and restart runtime workers on affected pools. Tertiary: Full node spin replacement with validated runtime image (runtime-1.22-hotfix).
coordination_matrix: Runtime owners: perform kernel selection fix and build hotfix images
Orchestrator: enforce model pin and stop rollout jobs
Console/Platform: push customer notifications and update public status page
SRE: monitor rollout and validate p95/p99 recovery

acceptance_criteria: All affected routes in Hosted/Dedicated/Private are pinned or reverted to v3.13 or validated hotfix by due_date
p99 latency under 350ms and hallucination metric back to pre-rollout baseline for three consecutive 24h periods
Automated rollout policy patched so auto_ramp respects per-tier constraints
open_questions: Why did quantized kernel selection differ only in mixed-precision path?
Can orchestration add a preflight test that runs long-context regression checks in canary?
Do we need a circuit-breaker to stop cross-environment auto-ramps when a hosted canary fails?
next_steps: Merge runtime hotfix and cut runtime-1.22.1 image
Ship orchestrator guardrail to block auto_ramp when hosted canaries show SLO regressions
Add a dedicated long-context unit in canary test harness and include semantic regression checks
Schedule cross-team postmortem review with CS and SRE on 2025-02-25
